spec.name: Accordion
spec.description: A stack of sections whose content expands and collapses under a heading, like an FAQ. Use with AccordionItem.

allowsMultipleExpanded.description: Lets several sections be open at once. Otherwise opening one closes the others.

defaultExpandedKeys.description: Sections open at first, by id, when uncontrolled.

isDisabled.description: Disables every section.

onExpandedChange.description: Called with the ids of the open sections.

children.description: AccordionItem elements.

keyboard: Tab moves between section headings
Enter or Space opens or closes the focused section
requirements: Each heading is a real heading (h3 by default) with a button inside, exposing aria-expanded
The button controls its panel (aria-controls), and the panel is labelled by the button
Collapsed content is removed from the tab order and hidden from screen readers
Expanding respects reduced motion
screenReader: Each section is announced as a heading and a button, collapsed or expanded
Opening a section announces it as expanded; its content follows in reading order
Headings appear in the screen reader's headings list, for quick navigation

use_when: FAQs and long help pages
Settings grouped into sections people rarely need all at once
avoid_when: Content everyone needs: show it
Switching between views of the same thing: use Tabs

Putting the only important information in a collapsed section

spec.name: AgentActivity
spec.description: A short summary of what the assistant is doing or did, such as "Used 3 tools", that opens into each step. It stays open while a step needs approval.

onApprove.description: Called with a tool's id when the person approves it.

onDeny.description: Called with a tool's id when the person declines it.

focusApproval.description: Move focus to an approval box when one appears.

keyboard: Enter / Space on the summary: shows or hides the steps
requirements: The summary is a button with aria-expanded that controls the list of steps
While any step is waiting for approval the list is forced open and the button is disabled: a question can't be hidden
Progress reads in words ("Working: 1 of 3 steps done"), failures and declines are counted
Each step is a ToolCall, so it announces its own changes
screenReader: "Used 3 tools (1 failed), button, collapsed"
While working: "Working: 1 of 3 steps done, button, collapsed"

use_when: Grouping the tool calls inside one reply
avoid_when: A single tool call: use ToolCall directly
anti_patterns: Collapsing the list while an approval is pending

spec.name: Alert
spec.description: An inline message about the state of the page or a task: a tip, a success, a warning or an error. For brief confirmations that disappear, use Toast.

children.description: The message. Say what happened and what to do next.

title.description: Optional bold first line, e.g. 'Payment failed'.

variant.description: Tone and urgency. Warning and danger interrupt a screen reader; info and success wait their turn.

onDismiss.description: When set, a close button appears and calls this. You remove the alert.

dismissLabel.description: Accessible name of the close button.

keyboard: Tab reaches the close button, when there is one
Enter or Space dismisses
requirements: Warning and danger use role=alert (announced at once); info and success use role=status (announced politely)
The tone is also said in words for screen readers (Warning:, Error:), and shown by an icon shape, never color alone
The icon is decorative (aria-hidden)
The close button has an accessible name and a visible focus ring
screenReader: A warning or error is announced as soon as it appears, prefixed with its tone
An info or success message is announced after the current speech finishes
The close button is announced as a button named Dismiss

use_when: A message tied to the page or a form that stays until it is fixed or dismissed
Explaining why something is disabled or failed
avoid_when: A short confirmation after an action: use Toast
A decision that blocks the user: use Dialog
An error on one field: use the field's own error message
anti_patterns: Several alerts stacked on one screen
Danger tone for something that is not an error
Rendering an alert that is already on screen again, which re-announces it

spec.name: ApprovalBox
spec.description: Asks someone to approve or decline something the assistant wants to do. It says what will happen, how risky it is and whether it can be undone, in words as well as color.

summary.description: What is about to happen, in plain words, e.g. "Delete 12 draft invoices".

risk.description: How much could go wrong. High risk uses the danger style and interrupts speech.

reversible.description: Whether the action can be undone. Unset says nothing about it.

approveLabel.description: Text of the approve button. Say the action: "Delete invoices" beats "OK".

isPending.description: True while the approval is being processed: shows a spinner and blocks a second press.

autoFocus.description: Move focus to the box when it appears, so a keyboard user lands on the question.

children.description: Extra detail, e.g. the list of items affected.

keyboard: Tab: moves between Deny and Approve
Enter / Space: presses the focused button
requirements: A named group: its name is the summary, so the question is read first
The box is announced when it appears (assertively for high risk, politely otherwise)
Focus goes to the box, not to a button, so a stray Enter can't approve something
Risk is shown as words ("High risk") and a different icon, not only by color
Deny comes first in the tab order; the approving button names the action
The caller is responsible for what happens to focus after an answer (ToolCall returns it to the tool)
screenReader: On appearing: "Approval needed: Delete 12 draft invoices. High risk. This can't be undone."
Then a group named by the summary, with the buttons Deny and Approve

use_when: The assistant needs permission before something that changes data, spends money or contacts someone
avoid_when: Asking about something trivial and reversible: just do it and offer undo
Collecting several fields: use a Dialog with a form
anti_patterns: Approval buttons labelled just OK and Cancel
Taking focus onto the approve button
Showing risk only with a red color

spec.name: Avatar
spec.description: A person's or account's picture, falling back to their initials when there is no image or it fails to load.

name.description: The person's name. It is the accessible name, and the source of the initials.

src.description: Image URL. If it is missing or fails to load, the initials show instead.

shape.description: Circle for people, square for organisations.

decorative.description: Hides it from screen readers, for when the name is already written next to it.

requirements: It is an image with the person's name as its text alternative
With decorative set, it is hidden from assistive technology so a name next to it isn't read twice
Initials text meets 4.5:1 against the background
screenReader: Announced as an image named after the person, e.g. "Ada Lovelace", unless decorative

use_when: Showing who wrote, owns or is assigned something
Account or user menus
avoid_when: A logo or product image: use an img

An empty name

variant.description: Tone: neutral for categories, the others for statuses.

requirements: The status is in the text, not only the color (a colored dot is decoration)

spec.name: BlurFade
spec.description: Content that sharpens and slides into place when it first appears or when it scrolls into view. It is visible to start with, so it never hides content from anyone.

children.description: The content to reveal.

delay.description: Seconds to wait before revealing. Stagger a list by giving each item a longer delay.

offset.description: How far, in pixels, it starts below its place.

blur.description: How blurred it starts, in pixels.

whenInView.description: Wait until it scrolls into view. Otherwise it reveals as soon as it mounts.

requirements: Decoration only: the animated layers are hidden from assistive technology and never take focus
Stands still for visitors who ask for less motion (prefers-reduced-motion), and the effect can also be shown still with the rdm-still class
Visible in the server-rendered page and without JavaScript; it is only hidden, before the first paint, once the browser can reveal it again
With reduced motion it is never hidden: it simply appears
The content is in the page and readable by assistive technology the whole time (opacity is not display:none)
Does not flash: nothing changes more than three times in a second (WCAG 2.3.1)
Optional: it is a separate component, so projects that do not add it carry none of its code
screenReader: Silent: the content is read in place as normal

use_when: Landing page sections, feature lists and cards that arrive as you scroll
Staggering the entrance of a short list
avoid_when: Content people need immediately, such as error messages or the main task of a page
Long lists: delays add up
anti_patterns: Delays over about half a second per item
Wrapping the whole page, so nothing is readable until it finishes

spec.name: Breadcrumbs
spec.description: The path from the top of the site to the current page, as links. Use BreadcrumbItem for each step; the last one is the current page.

children.description: BreadcrumbItem elements, from the top level down to the current page.

label.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Translate it for other languages.

isDisabled.description: Disables every link in the trail.

keyboard: Tab moves between the links
Enter follows a link
requirements: A navigation landmark with an accessible name, containing an ordered list of links
The last item is the current page: aria-current="page", and it cannot be followed (it has no href and is aria-disabled)
Separators are decorative (aria-hidden), so they are not read out
Links have a visible focus ring
screenReader: Announced as a navigation landmark named Breadcrumbs, with a list of N items
The final item is announced as the current page

use_when: Sites or apps with more than two levels of hierarchy
Telling people where they are and how to go back up
avoid_when: A flat site with one level: no trail is needed
Showing the steps someone has taken: use a stepper
anti_patterns: Making the current page a link to itself
Using breadcrumbs instead of the main navigation
Hiding the trail from screen readers with aria-hidden

spec.name: Button
spec.description: Triggers an action or event, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.

isDisabled.description: Prevents interaction and dims the button.

isLoading.description: Shows a spinner and blocks presses. The button stays focusable, is marked aria-disabled, and the pending state is announced.

children.description: Button label. Icon-only buttons must pass aria-label instead.

keyboard: Enter activates

Disabled: announced as unavailable or dimmed
Loading: announced as unavailable, and the busy state is spoken when loading starts

isDisabled.description: Disables every date.

keyboard: Arrow keys move by day and week
PageUp/PageDown change month, with Shift change year
Home/End jump to start/end of the week
Enter or Space selects

Unavailable dates are exposed as disabled

Each day announces its full date (Friday, 20 March 2026), plus selected or today
Dates outside min/max are announced as unavailable

spec.name: Card
spec.description: A bordered container that groups related content under an optional heading, with an optional footer for actions.

children.description: The card's content.

title.description: Heading shown at the top. Also names the card for screen readers.

footer.description: Actions or meta information along the bottom, e.g. buttons.

headingLevel.description: Heading level for the title, 2 to 6. Pick the level that fits where the card sits in the page's outline.

variant.description: outlined has a border, raised adds a shadow, subtle is a tinted block with no border.

requirements: With a title, the card is a group labelled by it; without one it is a plain container
The title is a real heading at the level you choose, so the page outline stays correct
A card is not a landmark and not focusable: put links and buttons inside it
screenReader: Entering a titled card announces its name and that it is a group
The title is reachable as a heading when navigating by headings

use_when: Grouping a small set of related facts or controls, like a plan, a project or a setting
A dashboard of independent blocks
avoid_when: Rows of the same record type: use a table or data grid
Wrapping a whole page

A heading level that skips (h1 then h4)
Making the whole card clickable and also putting buttons in it

spec.name: Chart
spec.description: A bar, line, area or donut chart drawn in plain SVG without a chart library. It fits its container, can be explored with a pointer or the arrow keys, and always comes with a written summary and a View as table switch that shows the same numbers.

data.description: The labels along the bottom and one or more named series of values. A donut draws the first series only.

summary.description: A sentence that tells the story of the chart. Defaults to a sentence written from the data.

type.description: Bars, a line, a filled area or a donut.

stacked.description: Add the series up instead of drawing them side by side. Applies to bar and area.

height.description: Height of the drawing in pixels. The width follows the container.

showLegend.description: Name each series (or each donut slice) below the drawing. Hidden for a single series except in a donut.

showGrid.description: Draw grid lines behind bar, line and area charts.

valueFormat.description: Turns a value into text for the axis, the tooltip, the labels and the table. Defaults to compact numbers with the data unit.

onSelect.description: Called when a point is clicked, or when Enter or Space is pressed on the active point.
onSelect.tsType: (point: { index: number; label: string; series: string; value: number }) => void

isLoading.description: Show a placeholder the size of the chart instead of the drawing.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when there is nothing to chart.

keyboard: Tab: moves to the plot, which is one tab stop
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: move to the previous or next value (ArrowUp / ArrowDown on a donut)
Home / End: jump to the first or last value
Escape: clears the active value
Enter / Space: selects the active value (calls onSelect)
requirements: The drawing is decoration; the title, the written summary and the data table carry the meaning
The plot is a single focusable group named by the title, described by the summary, with a visible focus ring
Moving with the keyboard announces the active value as text, for example "Feb: Revenue $26,500, Cost $12,000"
View as table swaps in the same data as an accessible table (aria-pressed on the switch)
Series differ by marker shape or label as well as color; the legend repeats the same marks
A donut names each slice with its percentage; slices are separated by a gap
Colors come only from the chart color tokens and text stays at 4.5:1
Loading is marked with aria-busy and shows no invented numbers
Empty data shows a message instead of an empty frame
screenReader: Announced as a figure named by the title, then the summary text
"Revenue by month. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between values, group"
Each arrow key press reads the active value, such as "Feb: Revenue $26,500, Cost $12,000"
"View as table, toggle button, not pressed"
The table reads every value under its row and column headers

use_when: Showing trends, comparisons or shares of a whole in a product screen
Letting people point at a value to read it exactly
avoid_when: Dashboards with many linked, zoomable charts: use a charting library
Exact numbers matter most: show a table
A single number with a trend: use Stat with a Sparkline
anti_patterns: A chart with no summary
Telling series apart by color only
A donut with many slices or with several series (it draws the first series only)
Hard-coding series colors instead of the chart color tokens

spec.name: Chat
spec.description: A whole conversation with an assistant: the messages, a box to write in, and the stop and jump-to-latest controls. It shows what you give it and reports what the person does; it never calls a model.

onSend.description: Called with the text and any attachments when the person sends a message or picks a suggestion.

onStop.description: Called when the person presses Stop while a reply is on its way.

onApprove.description: Called with a tool's id when the person approves it.

onDeny.description: Called with a tool's id when the person declines it.

onRetry.description: Shows Try again on the last message when it failed.

status.description: Where the conversation is: ready for input, waiting for the first words, streaming, or failed.

label.description: Accessible name of the chat.

suggestions.description: Prompts to offer when the chat is empty. Choosing one sends it.

headingLevel.description: Level of headings inside replies, 2 to 6.

attachments.description: Files added to the message being written. You own the list: add in onAttach, remove in onRemoveAttachment, clear it in onSend.

onAttach.description: Called with the chosen files. Providing it adds "Add photos & files" to the + menu and opens the file picker. Use fileToAttachment() to make attachments.

onRemoveAttachment.description: Called with an attachment's id when the person removes it. Without it the attachments have no remove button.

accept.description: Which files the picker offers, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".

actions.description: Extra entries for the + menu, such as Create image or Web search. Each has a label, an optional description and icon, and what to do when chosen.

onVoice.description: Shows a microphone button and calls this when it is pressed. Start or stop dictation yourself.

isListening.description: Dictation is on: the microphone button shows as pressed and its name becomes Stop dictation.

endContent.description: Your own controls on the right, before the microphone, for example a Think toggle.

keyboard: Tab: moves from the message list (focusable, so it can scroll with arrow keys) to the message box
Enter: sends; Shift+Enter: new line
Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down: scroll the messages when the list has focus
requirements: The message list is a log that is NOT live: streamed text would be read token by token
One polite status line says "Assistant is responding" and "Response complete"; tools announce their own changes
The list follows new text only while the reader is at the bottom; scrolling up stops it and shows Jump to latest
Only the newest unanswered approval takes focus
The message list is keyboard-scrollable (focusable) and has a visible focus ring
Sending always returns the view to the latest message
screenReader: "Chat, region", then "Chat messages, log"
After sending: "Assistant is responding", later "Response complete"
A tool needing approval: "Approval needed: <what>"

use_when: An assistant, copilot or agent conversation
Support chat with an AI
avoid_when: Chat between people with presence and typing: build on Message and PromptInput
anti_patterns: Making the whole list aria-live
Auto-scrolling while someone is reading earlier messages

with-tools
suggestions

spec.description: Lets the user turn a single option on or off, with an optional indeterminate state.

children.description: Visible label.

isIndeterminate.description: Shows a dash for a partially selected group, e.g. 'select all'.

isDisabled.description: Prevents interaction and dims the checkbox.

isInvalid.description: Marks the checkbox as invalid, e.g. an unaccepted required agreement.

onChange.description: Called with the new checked state.

keyboard: Space toggles
requirements: Label is part of the click target
Indeterminate is exposed as aria-checked=mixed

Toggling announces the new state
Invalid is announced as invalid

Selecting rows

Exactly one choice from a set: use RadioGroup
anti_patterns: Negative labels like 'Don't send emails'

href.description: Where the marker goes. Defaults to the matching entry in a Sources list on the same page.

spec.name: Combobox
spec.description: Text input that filters a list of options as you type. Supports multi-select tags, async loading and long, virtualized lists.

label.description: Visible label.

errorMessage.description: Shown when the field is invalid.

placeholder.description: Hint shown in the empty input.

selectionMode.description: multiple shows the chosen options as removable tags.

value.description: Controlled selection: one key (or null) in single mode, an array of keys in multiple mode.

allowsCustomValue.description: Lets the user keep text that doesn't match an option (single mode).

menuTrigger.description: What opens the list: typing, focusing, or only the button and arrow keys.

isLoading.description: Shows a spinner in the field, e.g. while an async search runs.

virtualized.description: Renders only visible options. Turn on for lists of more than a few hundred items.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when nothing matches the input.

isDisabled.description: Prevents interaction and dims the field.

isInvalid.description: Marks the field invalid and shows errorMessage.

isRequired.description: Requires a selection for form submission.

onLoadMore.description: Called when the user scrolls near the end of the list, for infinite loading.

keyboard: Typing filters the list
Down arrow opens the list; Up/Down arrows move through options
Enter selects, Esc closes and restores the input
Backspace in an empty input removes the last tag (multiple mode)

Each tag has a remove button named 'Remove <option>'
Loading state is announced
screenReader: On focus: the label, combo box, and collapsed or expanded
Typing announces the number of results or the focused option
Moving through options announces each option and its position; in the 5,000-item list, positions like 4,999 of 5,000
No matches: No results is announced
Async: Loading is announced while results load
Multiple: each tag's button is announced as Remove <option>; removing one with Backspace makes its removal clear

Rendering thousands of options without virtualized

Passing isInvalid for required or format checks (even isInvalid={false}): any defined value takes over validity and hides the built-in errors. Use isRequired and validate; pass isInvalid only for errors the app finds itself, such as from the server

spec.name: CommandPalette
spec.description: A search box in a dialog that finds and runs commands, jumps to pages and triggers actions from the keyboard. Opens with Ctrl or Cmd + K. Use CommandGroup and CommandItem for the results.

label.description: Accessible name of the dialog, e.g. "Command palette".

children.description: CommandGroup and CommandItem elements.

onOpenChange.description: Called when it opens or closes.

shortcut.description: Letter that opens it with Ctrl (Windows, Linux) or Cmd (Mac) held. Set null to turn the shortcut off and open it yourself.

onAction.description: Called with the id of any command run, in addition to the command's own onAction.

keyboard: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) opens it, and closes it when open
Typing filters the commands as you type
Up and Down arrows move through the results; Home and End jump to the first and last
Enter runs the highlighted command and closes the palette
Esc closes it and returns focus to where you were

Groups have visible headings that are also read to screen readers
When nothing matches, the empty message is announced
Shortcut hints on commands are display only, read after the command name
The backdrop blur is decoration; the dialog meets 4.5:1 contrast without it

Moving through results announces each command with its group and position
Typing announces the number of results, or that there are none
Running a command closes the dialog and focus returns to the page

The only way to reach important features

Commands whose names are not words people would search for
Not telling people the shortcut exists

spec.name: CustomerTable
spec.description: A ready-to-use customer list: search, filters, sorting, pages, CSV export, loading rows, an empty state, an error with retry, cards on a phone, and totals with a chart above that follow the filters. Give it customers and it works.

customers.description: The customers to show. With serverSide, only the current page.

label.description: Accessible name of the table and the section, e.g. "Customers".

currency.description: ISO currency code for revenue, e.g. "USD" or "EUR".

locale.description: Locale for numbers and dates, e.g. "en-GB". Defaults to the visitor's.

isLoading.description: Show loading rows and skeleton cards, disable the controls, and mark the section busy.

error.description: A message to show instead of the list when loading failed.

onRetry.description: Adds a Try again button to the error message.

insights.description: The totals and chart above the table. "auto" works them out from the customers and follows the filters (not with serverSide); "none" hides them; or pass your own numbers.

serverSide.description: The list lives on a server. The table then shows exactly the customers you pass, and asks for new ones through onQueryChange when the search, a filter, the sort or the page changes.

totalCount.description: With serverSide: how many customers match in all, so the pages and the count are right.

onQueryChange.description: With serverSide: called with the new query (search, status, plan, sort, page, pageSize). Typing in the search waits for a short pause first.

defaultQuery.description: Start with a search, filters, a sort or a page already set.

onExport.description: Replaces the built-in CSV download. It gets the customers that match (all pages when the list is in memory). With serverSide the Export button is shown only when you provide this.

onOpenCustomer.description: Makes each name a button and calls this with the customer, e.g. to open a details panel.

statusTones.description: Which badge color a status gets. The defaults are active green, trial blue, overdue amber, churned red; anything else is neutral.

keyboard: Tab: moves through the search, the filters, Export, the table (one stop), the names when onOpenCustomer is set, and the page buttons
In the table: arrow keys move between cells; Enter or Space on a column header sorts
In a filter: Enter or Space opens the list, arrow keys choose, Escape closes
Escape in the search box clears it
requirements: A labelled region around everything; the table and the phone cards have their own names
A real table with a row header (the customer), sortable column headers that expose their sort direction, and right-aligned money in tabular numerals
The count of matching customers is a polite status message, so filtering is announced; so is an export ("Exported 24 customers to customers.csv")
Search and filters each have a name (read, not drawn); the status of a customer is always text in a badge, never a color alone
Loading marks the region busy and shows skeletons instead of fake numbers; the controls are disabled while loading
An empty list says why (nothing yet, or nothing matches) and offers Clear filters; an error is an alert with a retry button

spec.name: DataGrid
spec.description: A fast, accessible data grid for thousands of rows: sorting, filtering, grouping, editing, copy and paste, export and server-side data. Columns are TanStack Table column definitions.

label.description: Accessible name of the grid, e.g. 'Orders'.

data.description: Rows to show. Keep the array reference stable between renders.

columns.description: TanStack Table column definitions. Give each column an id or accessorKey.

getRowId.description: Stable id per row. Needed for selection to survive sorting and filtering.

height.description: Height of the scrolling area in px.

virtualized.description: Renders only visible rows. Keeps 100k rows fast.

sortable.description: Lets users sort by clicking or pressing Enter on a header. Shift adds a secondary sort.

selectionMode.description: Adds a checkbox column and Space-to-select.

onSelectionChange.description: Called with the selected row ids.

globalFilter.description: Shows only rows where some cell contains this text (case-insensitive).

resizableColumns.description: Drag a header edge, or press Alt+Left/Right on a header, to resize.

pinnedColumns.description: Column ids kept visible on the left while scrolling sideways.

showColumnFilters.description: Adds a filter row under the header. Set meta.filter on a column to 'text', 'select' or false.

pageSize.description: Rows per page. When set, a pager is shown; when not, all rows scroll (virtualized).

onCellEdit.description: Called when the user saves an edit in a column with meta.editable. Update your data to apply it.

onCellsEdit.description: Called once with every cell a paste changes. Prefer it to onCellEdit when you paste: applying a whole paste in one update avoids state updates overwriting each other. When it isn't set, a paste calls onCellEdit once per cell.

rangeSelection.description: Select a block of cells with Shift+arrows, Shift+click or by dragging. Ctrl+C copies it as spreadsheet-ready text; Ctrl+V pastes into editable cells.

apiRef.description: Gives you getCsv(), downloadCsv() and downloadExcel() for the rows that pass the filters. Create it with useRef<DataGridApi>(null).

serverSide.description: Your server does the sorting, filtering and paging. The grid shows the rows you pass (one page), reports what the user asked for through onQueryChange, and uses rowCount for the pager. Needs pageSize. Not combined with groupBy or getSubRows.

rowCount.description: serverSide: total rows on the server across all pages, after the current search and filters.

onQueryChange.description: serverSide: called on mount and whenever the sort, filters, search or page change. Typing in a filter waits queryDelay ms; sorting and paging fire at once. Fetch, then pass the new data, rowCount and isLoading.

queryDelay.description: serverSide: milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke in a filter or search before calling onQueryChange.

fillHandle.description: A small handle on the corner of the selection: drag it to fill the cells it covers, continuing numbers (2, 4 gives 6, 8), text that ends in a number (Item 1 gives Item 2), ISO dates and otherwise repeating the values. Ctrl+D and Ctrl+R fill down and right from the keyboard. Needs rangeSelection and an edit handler (onCellEdit or onCellsEdit); only editable cells are written.

columnMenu.description: Adds a menu to every column header: sort, pin, reset width, hide, and show hidden columns again. Alt+Down, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a header opens it.

rowReorder.description: Adds a drag handle column. Rows can be dragged, or moved with Alt+Up and Alt+Down. The grid reports the move through onRowReorder; you reorder your data. Off while sorting, filtering, grouping or serverSide is in use, because the rows are no longer in your data's order.

onRowReorder.description: Called with { rowId, fromIndex, toIndex } when a row is moved. Apply it with reorderRows(rows, move).

isLoading.description: Marks the grid busy and shows a loading message.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when there are no rows to display.

onRowAction.description: Called on Enter or double-click on a row, e.g. to open details.

onFilteredDataChange.description: Called with the rows that match the search and column filters, in display order, whenever they change. Use it for counts and totals.

groupBy.description: Column ids to group rows by, outermost first. Group rows show the value, a row count, and a total in each column that sets aggregationFn ('sum', 'mean', 'min', 'max', 'count', 'uniqueCount' or a function).

defaultExpanded.description: Start with every group, tree row and detail panel open.

getSubRows.description: Tree data: returns a row's children. Rows with children get an expand toggle and are indented by depth. Search keeps a parent when a child matches.

renderDetail.description: Master-detail: content shown in a panel under a row when it's expanded.

detailHeight.description: Height of each detail panel in px; the panel scrolls if its content is taller.

Arrow keys move between cells, including the header row
Home/End move to the first/last cell in the row
Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End move to the first/last cell in the grid
PageUp/PageDown move by one screen of rows
Enter or Space on a header sorts; with Shift it adds a secondary sort
Alt+Left/Right on a header resizes the column
Space on a row toggles its selection; Ctrl+A selects all (multiple mode)
Enter on a row calls onRowAction
Enter or F2 on an editable cell starts editing; typing a character starts editing with it, including the first key of an IME (Japanese, Chinese, Korean input)
While editing, Enter saves and Escape cancels; focus returns to the cell
Enter or typing on a filter cell moves into its filter; Escape returns to the grid
On a group, tree or detail row, Right arrow in the toggle cell expands it and Left arrow collapses it; Enter on a group row (or on the toggle cell, when it isn't editable) toggles it
Space on a group row selects or clears all its rows (multiple mode)
Shift+arrows, Shift+Home/End and Shift+PageUp/PageDown extend a block of cells from the cell you started on; Escape clears it
Ctrl+C (Cmd+C) copies the block as tab-separated text, the way it is shown; with no block it copies the focused cell
Ctrl+V (Cmd+V) pastes spreadsheet text into editable cells from the focused cell; one copied value fills a selected block

Grid has an accessible name

Selected rows expose aria-selected
Only one cell is in the tab order at a time (roving tabindex)
Filter inputs and editors are labelled with their column name
Pager announces the visible row range

Cells in a selected block expose aria-selected, and a polite status announces how many cells are selected, copied or pasted
screenReader: Entering the grid announces its name and size (rows and columns)
Moving across announces each column header; moving down announces row numbers from the full dataset (row 50,000 of 100,001), even though rows are virtualized
Sorting with Enter announces the new sort direction on that header
Selected rows are announced as selected

Editing: Enter opens an edit field announced as Edit <column>; after Enter, the saved value is read
The pager's range (Rows 11–20 of 237) is announced after changing page

avoid_when: A few items with rich layout: use a list or cards

spec.name: PromptInput
spec.description: The message box of a chat: one rounded bar with a + menu on the left, the text in the middle, and your own controls, a microphone and Send on the right. Added files show above the text. You get only the buttons you ask for.

onSubmit.description: Called with the trimmed text and the attachments when the person sends. A message with files and no text can be sent.

onStop.description: Called when the person presses Stop.

isStreaming.description: A reply is on its way: the button becomes Stop and sending is blocked.

isDisabled.description: Stop all input.

placeholder.description: Hint shown while the box is empty.

label.description: Accessible name of the text box.

value.description: Controlled text. Leave out to let the box keep its own.

attachments.description: Files added to the message but not sent yet. You own the list: add to it in onAttach, remove from it in onRemoveAttachment. Images show as small pictures, other files as chips.

onAttach.description: Called with the chosen files. Providing it adds "Add photos & files" to the + menu and opens the file picker. Use fileToAttachment() to make attachments.

onRemoveAttachment.description: Called with an attachment's id when the person removes it. Without it the attachments have no remove button.

accept.description: Which files the picker offers, e.g. "image/*,.pdf".

actions.description: Extra entries for the + menu, such as Create image or Web search. Each has a label, an optional description and icon, and what to do when chosen.

onVoice.description: Shows a microphone button and calls this when it is pressed. Start or stop dictation yourself.

isListening.description: Dictation is on: the microphone button shows as pressed and its name becomes Stop dictation.

endContent.description: Your own controls on the right, before the microphone, for example a Think toggle.

Shift+Enter: new line
Tab: moves through the + button, the text, your controls, the microphone and Send

requirements: A real labelled multi-line text box; the shortcut hint is attached with aria-describedby (read by assistive technology, not drawn)
Enter does nothing while an input method (IME) is composing, so a half-typed word can't be sent
Send is disabled when there is no text and no file; Stop replaces it while streaming and has its own name
The + button is a menu button named "Add attachments or tools"; its menu has a name and every entry has a text label
Attachments are a labelled list; every remove button names its file ("Remove photo.png"); adding and removing is announced politely; an image's alt text is its file name
Only pictures from this device (blob: or data: addresses) are drawn: nothing is loaded from a remote address
The microphone button is a toggle (aria-pressed) whose name changes to Stop dictation
When the text grows past a line the bar becomes two rows without moving the text box in the page, so typing and focus are never interrupted
Focus stays in the text box after sending, attaching or removing a file
Growth stops at a maximum height, then the box scrolls
screenReader: "Message, edit text, multi-line. Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line"
"Add attachments or tools, menu button", then the entries such as "Add photos & files"
After choosing files: "Added photo.png"; the list reads "Attachments, list, 1 item" and "Remove photo.png, button"
"Send message, button, dimmed" while empty; "Stop generating, button" while streaming

avoid_when: A short single-line field: use TextField
anti_patterns: Sending on Enter without checking for IME composition
Clearing the box before the message is sent

spec.name: Response
spec.description: Shows an assistant's reply as formatted text: headings, lists, tables, code, links and source markers. It is safe for text you do not control and for text that is still arriving.

children.description: The reply, as markdown.

isStreaming.description: True while the reply is still arriving. Shows a caret and tells assistive technology the content is changing.

A copy button reads as, e.g. "Copy typescript code", then "Copied to clipboard"
Source markers read as "Source 2: <title>"

Any markdown from a source you can't fully trust
avoid_when: Authoring or editing markdown: this only displays it
Showing a user's own message: use plain text

Re-mounting the component on every streamed chunk instead of updating its text
